_comment: Surface (ADT/protein) marker panel for functional-state scoring. Run with assay='ADT'. Markers are written in canonical form; '_aliases' below maps each to the other names vendors use, so one file works across panels. Add a line to _aliases when a new panel names something differently. Keys starting with '_' are not states.

naive-like.description: Naive: CD62L+ CCR7+ CD45RA+ CD27+ and CD95-LOW. CD95 is the discriminator against TSCM and virtual memory, which are otherwise naive by surface phenotype - so CD95 is deliberately NOT listed here; its absence is the evidence.

references.title: Guidelines for T cell nomenclature
references.authors: Masopust D, Soerens AG, Quarnstrom CF, Ahmed R, et al.
references.note: Surface markers per the consensus guidelines and companion poster (10.1038/s41577-025-01246-2).

curation_notes: Review 2026-08-10, no removals: CD31 (PECAM1) marks recent thymic emigrants within CD4 naive only; CXCR4 is broadly expressed but naive-enriched. Both additional-tier.

memory.description: Memory. TCM CD62L+CCR7+CD45RO+; TEM CD62L-CCR7-; TEMRA re-expresses CD45RA with KLRG1/CX3CR1/CD16; TRM CD103+CD69+CD49a+; TSCM CD95+CD28+CD127+ on a CD45RA+ background.

references.title: Guidelines for T cell nomenclature
references.authors: Masopust D, Soerens AG, Quarnstrom CF, Ahmed R, et al.
references.note: Surface markers per the consensus guidelines and companion poster (10.1038/s41577-025-01246-2).

curation_notes: Review 2026-08-10, no removals. FLAG for expert: human CD44 is high on essentially all T cells (a mouse-derived discriminator, weak on human panels); CD122 is shared with the virtual-memory core.

virtual-memory.description: Virtual memory (TVM): naive T cells that proliferated WITHOUT cognate antigen, giving antigen-experience markers on a naive backbone. Consensus TVM lineage markers are CD44-hi CD122-hi CD49d-LOW with high EOMES (Eomes binds the IL2RB/CD122 promoter). CD49d is deliberately NOT scored: it is a LOW marker and UCell is additive on presence. CD95 sits in additional, not core - it is shared with TSCM and is not TVM-defining. TVM is described as a CD8 population; treat calls on CD4 cells as unsupported.

references.title: Guidelines for T cell nomenclature
references.authors: Masopust D, Soerens AG, Quarnstrom CF, Ahmed R, et al.
references.note: Surface markers per the consensus guidelines and companion poster (10.1038/s41577-025-01246-2).

activated.description: Acute activation: CD69 earliest, then CD25/CD38/HLA-DR and co-stimulatory TNFRSF members. CD69 is also a residency marker - read with CD103 before calling activation in tissue. The guidelines note 'activated' is often used as a synonym for 'effector' but carries fewer inferences about fate or longevity.

references.title: Guidelines for T cell nomenclature
references.authors: Masopust D, Soerens AG, Quarnstrom CF, Ahmed R, et al.
references.note: Surface markers per the consensus guidelines and companion poster (10.1038/s41577-025-01246-2).

curation_notes: Review 2026-08-10, no removals. FLAG for expert: CD27 is constitutive on naive/memory and LOST on terminal effectors, so it is not activation-specific - kept in additional because acute activation transiently upregulates it; CD71 (TFRC, added to _aliases) is a solid activation/proliferation marker.

exhaustion.description: Progressive exhaustion. TPEX are CXCR5+ PD-1-intermediate and retain proliferative capacity; TEX-term are CD101+CD38+ with dense co-inhibitory expression and low CD127. Requires chronic antigen - not inferable from PD-1 alone, which is also an activation marker.

references.title: Guidelines for T cell nomenclature
references.authors: Masopust D, Soerens AG, Quarnstrom CF, Ahmed R, et al.
references.note: Surface markers per the consensus guidelines and companion poster (10.1038/s41577-025-01246-2).

curation_notes: Inversion sweep 2026-08-10: removed CD127 - exhausted T cells are CD127-LOW (the description itself says TEX-term have low CD127); scoring it rewards naive/memory cells. This is the addendum's predicted inversion. Removed BTLA - highest on naive CD8 and downregulated with progressive differentiation (Baitsch/Derre, JCI 2010); tumour-specific TILs can re-express it, but for a general classifier it is naive-weighted. Client panel note: TIM3 is absent from the client's 161-marker panel, so core scores on 4 markers there.

regulating.description: Treg: CD25-HIGH plus CTLA-4 and the CD39/CD73 adenosine axis. The defining CD127-LOW half of the phenotype is deliberately NOT scored: UCell signatures are additive on presence, so a low/negative marker would reward exactly the wrong cells. FOXP3 is likewise absent - intracellular, never on a surface panel. This state is therefore weaker on ADT than RNA; corroborate with the RNA file.

references.title: Guidelines for T cell nomenclature
references.authors: Masopust D, Soerens AG, Quarnstrom CF, Ahmed R, et al.
references.note: Surface markers per the consensus guidelines and companion poster (10.1038/s41577-025-01246-2).

curation_notes: Review 2026-08-10, no removals. FLAG for expert: human Tregs are largely CD73-low at the protein level (CD39/CD73 co-expression is a mouse-weighted expectation); CD15s marks the most suppressive effector Tregs but is panel-dependent.

cytotoxicity.description: Cytotoxic effector phenotype. This state also covers the consensus 'effector' differentiation state: Table 1 defines effector by effector MOLECULES (granzyme B, perforin, CD40L), which on a surface panel are visible only as CD107a degranulation and CD40L. A separate 'effector' state would duplicate this one and split which.max between two near-identical signatures.

references.title: Guidelines for T cell nomenclature
references.authors: Masopust D, Soerens AG, Quarnstrom CF, Ahmed R, et al.
references.note: Surface markers per the consensus guidelines and companion poster (10.1038/s41577-025-01246-2).

curation_notes: Review 2026-08-10, no removals. FLAG for expert: CD94 (KLRD1) pairs with inhibitory NKG2A as often as activating NKG2C and is NK-weighted; CD11b on T cells marks only a small effector CD8 subset and is otherwise myeloid; CD107a (LAMP1) reports degranulation and is surface-visible mainly after stimulation, so it contributes little on resting cells. All three are additional-tier.

anergy.description: Anergy: hyporesponsive despite antigen. CD5-high with PD-1 but WITHOUT CD25/CD69 separates anergy from activation. FR4 (folate receptor 4), the classic partner to CD73, is mouse literature and absent from human panels - dropped for that reason.

references.title: Guidelines for T cell nomenclature
references.authors: Masopust D, Soerens AG, Quarnstrom CF, Ahmed R, et al.
references.note: Surface markers per the consensus guidelines and companion poster (10.1038/s41577-025-01246-2).

curation_notes: Inversion sweep 2026-08-10: removed CD25 and CD69 - this state's own description defines anergy as PD-1+ WITHOUT CD25/CD69; scoring them positively rewarded exactly the activated cells anergy must be separated from. FLAG for expert: CD5 is on all T cells (anergy uses CD5-HIGH, a shift rather than presence/absence), so it is a weak discriminator in a rank-based scorer - kept so core does not fall to two markers.
